title: ImageToKitty never chunked payloads over the protocol's 4096-byte limit
description:
Found via manual testing immediately after fixing bmd-wt6 (colon vs semicolon separator): a real image (kitten illustration, ~587KB base64-encoded) still failed to render in a real Kitty terminal, again with no error -- this time showing the raw base64 payload as literal wrapped text filling the screen.

Root cause confirmed against the official Kitty graphics protocol spec: base64 payload must be split into chunks no larger than 4096 bytes each, with m=1 marking every chunk but the last (m=0). ImageToKitty always sent the entire payload as a single m=0 ('final, no more chunks') command regardless of size -- any real photo/screenshot is virtually always over 4096 bytes once base64-encoded, so this was a near-100%-of-the-time failure for real images, not an edge case.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a document with any real-world-sized local image in a real Kitty terminal renders correctly, with the base64 payload properly split across multiple chunked escape sequences per the protocol's 4096-byte-per-chunk limit.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run bmd inside a real Kitty terminal (with bmd-wt6's separator fix already applied).
2. Open a doc referencing a real-world-sized image (e.g. test-data/singlerepo-referenced-docs/sample-image.png, ~440KB).
Result (pre-fix): raw base64-looking garbage text fills the screen instead of an image.

## Fix
Rewrote ImageToKitty (internal/renderer/images.go) to split the base64 payload into <=4096-byte chunks, emitting one escape sequence per chunk: only the first carries the full control-data set (a=T,f=100,...), subsequent chunks carry only m=, and every chunk but the last is marked m=1 (more chunks follow).
close_reason:
Root cause confirmed against the official Kitty graphics protocol spec: base64 payload must be split into chunks no larger than 4096 bytes each, with m=1 marking every chunk but the last (m=0 on the final one), and only the first chunk carrying the full control-data set. ImageToKitty always sent the entire payload as a single m=0 command regardless of size -- any real photo/screenshot is virtually always over 4096 bytes once base64-encoded, so this failed for essentially all real images, not an edge case.

Fixed: rewrote ImageToKitty (internal/renderer/images.go) to split the base64 payload into <=4096-byte chunks, one escape sequence per chunk (first chunk carries the full control set, subsequent chunks carry only m=). Added TestImageToKitty_ChunksLargePayloads (internal/renderer/renderer_test.go), which verifies chunk count, m=0/m=1 marking, that only the first chunk has the full control set, and that reassembling all chunks reproduces the exact original base64 data. Also updated TestView_KittyProtocolImage_NoWrapCorruption (bmd-t0o) to check every chunk (not just the first) for wrap-corruption, since a 50000-byte test image now correctly chunks into multiple sequences. Full suite green, go vet/gofmt clean.

title: ImageToKitty used wrong separator (: instead of ;), silently failing in real Kitty terminals
description:
Found via manual testing: after fixing the OSC/APC wrap-corruption bug (bmd-t0o), opening an image doc in a real Kitty terminal still showed no image at all -- not even a placeholder or error, just silently missing.

Root cause confirmed against the official Kitty graphics protocol spec (sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/graphics-protocol/): 'All graphics escape codes are of the form: <ESC>_G<control data>;<payload><ESC>\' -- the control-data key=value list and the base64 payload must be separated by a semicolon. internal/renderer/images.go's ImageToKitty() used a colon instead: '\x1b_Ga=T,f=100,m=0:%s\x1b\\'. With the wrong separator, a real Kitty terminal never finds the control-data boundary it expects, so the entire command silently fails to parse and nothing is displayed -- no error, no fallback text, just a missing image.

This is a genuinely pre-existing bug (predates all block-art/Alacritty/Terminal.app work this session) -- the function's own comment ('Alacritty will scale to fit') suggests it was written/tested under the mistaken assumption that Alacritty supports the Kitty protocol (confirmed false earlier this session), so it's plausible this code path was never actually validated against a real Kitty-protocol-supporting terminal before now.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a document with a local image in a real Kitty terminal (KITTY_WINDOW_ID set) renders the image correctly via the Kitty graphics protocol, matching the official spec's escape sequence format exactly.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run bmd inside a real Kitty terminal.
2. Open a markdown doc referencing a local image (e.g. test-data/singlerepo-referenced-docs/readme.md).
Result (pre-fix): no image renders, no placeholder text, nothing -- the doc looks exactly as if the image markdown didn't exist.

## Fix
Changed the separator from ':' to ';' in ImageToKitty() (internal/renderer/images.go), matching the official protocol spec exactly. Also corrected a stale comment claiming Alacritty supports the Kitty protocol (confirmed false via research earlier this session -- see bmd-qmb).
close_reason:
Root cause confirmed against the official Kitty graphics protocol spec (sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/graphics-protocol/), which states control data and payload are separated by a semicolon: '<ESC>_G<control data>;<payload><ESC>\'. ImageToKitty() (internal/renderer/images.go) used a colon instead, so a real Kitty terminal never found the expected boundary and the whole command silently failed to parse -- no error, no image, no fallback text.

This predates all block-art/Alacritty/Terminal.app work this session -- the function's own comment ('Alacritty will scale to fit') suggests it was written under the mistaken assumption that Alacritty supports the Kitty protocol (confirmed false earlier this session via bmd-qmb's research), so this code path was plausibly never actually validated against a real Kitty terminal before now.

Fixed: changed the separator from ':' to ';', matching the spec exactly. Corrected the stale Alacritty-support comment too. Added TestImageToKitty_UsesSemicolonSeparator (internal/renderer/renderer_test.go), verified via revert-and-rerun: fails against the pre-fix code with the exact malformed sequence ('\x1b_Ga=T,f=100,m=0:...' instead of '...m=0;...'), passes with the fix. Also updated TestView_KittyProtocolImage_NoWrapCorruption's (bmd-t0o) hardcoded expected prefix to match the corrected separator. Full suite green, go vet/gofmt clean.

title: Line-wrapping/truncation utilities corrupted OSC/APC inline-image escape sequences (Kitty graphics protocol)
description:
Found via manual testing: opening a doc with an image in the Kitty terminal (real Kitty graphics protocol support) produced a wall of garbled base64-looking text filling the entire screen instead of an image.

Root cause: wrapLineToWidth() (internal/tui/viewer.go, the main non-split-pane viewer's line-wrapping function) and the stripANSI() it calls (internal/tui/selection.go) only recognized CSI escape sequences (\x1b[...m) -- the format used for SGR color codes. Inline image protocols use different formats entirely: iTerm2 uses OSC (\x1b]...terminated by BEL or ST), Kitty uses APC (\x1b_...terminated by ST). Worse than just failing to recognize them: their embedded base64 payload can incidentally contain a literal 'm' character very early in the sequence (e.g. Kitty's own control-key syntax 'f=100,m=0:' contains one), so the CSI-only scanner stopped there, treating everything after as literal 'plain' text -- massively over-measuring the line's length and triggering wrapLineToWidth's hard-wrap logic, which then re-scanned the SAME way and inserted a newline every maxWidth runes through the entire base64 payload, corrupting the escape sequence and leaking raw image data as garbage text across many terminal rows.

The exact same CSI-only assumption existed independently in ansiPadOrTruncate() and insertCursorAtVisual() (both in viewer.go) -- the latter is used for the mouse-hover-cursor overlay in view mode (fixed for a related but distinct bug, bmd-zag, earlier this session), so hovering over an image line could also trigger this. stripInlineImageEscapes() (added for bmd-uc6) also only recognized OSC, not APC, leaving Kitty images vulnerable in the legacy viewWithBrowser split too.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a document containing an image in any terminal (Kitty, iTerm2, Alacritty/Terminal.app via the Braille fallback) never produces a garbled wall of text -- the image escape sequence (or its rendered equivalent) survives fully intact regardless of terminal width or line-wrapping.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run bmd inside a real Kitty terminal (KITTY_WINDOW_ID set, or TERM=xterm-kitty).
2. Open a markdown doc referencing a reasonably large local image (e.g. test-data/singlerepo-referenced-docs/readme.md).
Result (pre-fix): the terminal fills with what looks like base64-encoded garbage text wrapped at the terminal width, instead of an image.

## Fix
Added a single shared ansiEscapeRuneLen() helper (internal/tui/selection.go) that correctly measures the full extent of CSI, OSC, APC, and DCS escape sequences (recognizing their actual terminators -- BEL or ST for OSC/APC/DCS -- rather than scanning for a literal 'm'), and rewired stripANSI, wrapLineToWidth, ansiPadOrTruncate, insertCursorAtVisual, and stripInlineImageEscapes to all use it consistently instead of each having its own ad-hoc CSI-only escape detection.
close_reason:
Root cause confirmed via direct reproduction and revert-and-rerun testing: wrapLineToWidth() (internal/tui/viewer.go) and the stripANSI() it relied on (internal/tui/selection.go) only recognized CSI escape sequences (\x1b[...m). Kitty's graphics protocol uses APC (\x1b_...ST) and iTerm2 uses OSC (\x1b]...BEL/ST); both formats' embedded base64 payload can incidentally contain a literal 'm' character very early on (Kitty's own control syntax 'f=100,m=0:' has one), so the CSI-only scanner stopped there and mis-measured the line as enormous, triggering wrapLineToWidth's hard-wrap logic to insert a newline every maxWidth runes through the entire base64 payload -- corrupting the escape sequence and leaking raw image data as garbage text.

The same CSI-only assumption existed independently in ansiPadOrTruncate() and insertCursorAtVisual() (the latter used for the view-mode mouse-hover-cursor overlay, so hovering over an image line was also vulnerable), and stripInlineImageEscapes() (bmd-uc6) only recognized OSC, not APC, leaving Kitty images vulnerable in the legacy viewWithBrowser split too.

Fixed with one shared, correct primitive: ansiEscapeRuneLen() (internal/tui/selection.go) measures the full extent of CSI, OSC, APC, and DCS sequences using their real terminators (BEL or ST for OSC/APC/DCS, not a literal-'m' scan), and stripANSI/wrapLineToWidth/ansiPadOrTruncate/insertCursorAtVisual/stripInlineImageEscapes were all rewired to use it instead of five independent ad-hoc CSI-only implementations.

Verified via revert-and-rerun: TestView_KittyProtocolImage_NoWrapCorruption (internal/tui/viewer_test.go) fails against the pre-fix code with a 67518-byte segment containing an embedded newline (exact wrap corruption), and passes with the fix. Added TestStripANSI_HandlesOSCAndAPCSequences and TestAnsiEscapeRuneLen_ExactBoundaries (internal/tui/selection_test.go) for direct unit coverage of the shared helper, including the exact 'incidental m in payload' scenario that caused the original bug. Full suite green, go vet/gofmt clean.

title: Copy-selection and copy-line clipboard actions leaked raw ANSI escape fragments
description:
Found via manual testing during this session (user pasted a screenshot of copied clipboard content showing literal escape-code fragments). Selecting text via click-drag and copying it with Ctrl+C (the 'Selection copied' status message path) produced copied text containing raw ANSI escape bytes/fragments instead of clean plain text — observed clipboard content: "[38;5;141m• [0mSee [4m[38;5;141move" instead of the intended "See overview.md for system context".

Root cause: getSelectedText() (internal/tui/selection.go) sliced Viewer.Lines directly using SelectionPoint.ColumnIndex values, which are visual/screen column positions (derived from mouse msg.X). But Viewer.Lines is NOT plain text — stripAllSentinels() only removes internal link-tracking sentinels, leaving the renderer's full ANSI color/underline/bold escape codes intact. Slicing an ANSI-laden string by a visual column index lands mid-escape-sequence, since invisible escape-code runes are interleaved with visible character runes.

Also found and fixed the sibling 'copy line to clipboard' path (viewer.go ctrl+c handler, no-selection/hasCursor branch): it copied v.Lines[v.cursorRow] directly (mislabeled as 'plainLine' in a comment) with zero ANSI stripping, so a whole-line copy would paste complete but literal escape codes.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting text (drag) across any styled/linked line and copying it via Ctrl+C yields clean plain text with no ANSI escape bytes or bracket-code fragments, matching the plain-text rendering exactly at the same visual column range. Copying the committed-cursor line similarly yields ANSI-free plain text.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open a markdown doc with a bulleted list containing a link (e.g. test-data/singlerepo-referenced-docs/auth.md: '- See [overview.md](overview.md) for system context').
2. Click-drag to select text spanning that bullet/link line.
3. Press Ctrl+C to copy the selection.
4. Paste the clipboard contents somewhere and observe literal ANSI escape-code fragments (e.g. bracket-number-m sequences) mixed into the text instead of clean plain text.

Alternate repro for the sibling 'copy line' bug: click a line (no drag) to commit a cursor, press Ctrl+C with no active selection — the whole line is copied with embedded ANSI codes rather than as plain text.
close_reason:
Root cause confirmed via direct reproduction: getSelectedText() (internal/tui/selection.go) sliced Viewer.Lines directly using SelectionPoint.ColumnIndex (a visual/screen column from mouse msg.X), but Viewer.Lines still carries the renderer's full ANSI styling — stripAllSentinels() only removes link-tracking sentinels, not color/underline codes. Indexing an ANSI-laden string by a visual column lands mid-escape-sequence.

Fixed by having getSelectedText() strip ANSI from each line (stripANSI) before slicing it, for all three code paths (single-line, multi-line first/middle/last). Also fixed the sibling 'copy line to clipboard' path (viewer.go ctrl+c handler) which copied v.Lines[v.cursorRow] raw with zero stripping despite being commented 'plain text' — now wrapped in stripANSI() too.

Verified via revert-and-rerun: TestSelection_CopiedTextHasNoRawAnsiFragments (internal/tui/mouse_test.go) fails against the pre-fix code with the exact corruption pattern the user reported ("\x1b[38;5;39m• \x1b[0mSee \x1b[4m\x1b[38" — same structure as the user's observed "[38;5;141m• [0mSee [4m[38;5;141move", just a different theme color number), and passes with the fix. Full suite green, go vet/gofmt clean.

title: Text selection drag over a link line triggers navigation; return leaves a raw ANSI escape leaking into rendered text
description: In view mode, attempting to click-drag to select text on a line that also contains a rendered link causes bmd to follow the link instead of starting/extending a text selection. After navigating back (Ctrl+B or h), the returned-to document renders with a raw, unescaped ANSI code fragment visible as literal text (observed: '141mPayment Processing' where the leading ESC byte / [38;5; prefix is missing, leaving only the fragment 141m and the reset sequence visible as garbage before the item text) instead of properly color-styling the bullet list item. Screenshot captured during manual verification of v1.1.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open a doc with a bulleted list where list items are links (e.g. test-data/singlerepo-referenced-docs/overview.md).
2. Click-drag across a line containing a rendered link (e.g. "Payment Processing") attempting to select its text.
Result A: bmd follows the link and navigates to the linked page instead of starting a text selection.
3. Navigate back (Ctrl+B or h) to the originating document.
Result B: the returned-to document's rendering is corrupted — a raw ANSI escape fragment ("141m") leaks into the visible text before "Payment Processing" instead of being interpreted as a color code, and the link's underline/highlight styling is lost on that line while sibling link lines (User Authentication, Notifications, Analytics) still render correctly styled.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Click-dragging over a link-containing line starts/extends a text selection like any other line; it does not trigger follow-link navigation (mouse-down alone on a link may still follow it, per existing click-to-follow behavior, but a drag/select gesture must not).
2. After navigating back to a document via history (Ctrl+B/h), every line re-renders identically to its first-render state — no raw escape-sequence fragments leak into visible text, and link styling is preserved on every link line.
close_reason:
Two distinct root causes found via direct reproduction:

(a) Drag-vs-click: updateMouse's MouseActionPress handler followed any link line immediately on mouse-down, with no way to distinguish a click from the start of a drag. Fixed by deferring the follow to MouseActionRelease: Press now queues the link (Viewer.pendingLinkURL) and always starts a selection as before; Motion sets Viewer.mouseDragged=true if the point moves off the press point (canceling the pending follow); Release fires the queued follow only if no drag occurred, otherwise the in-progress selection stands. Confirmed tea.WithMouseCellMotion() (cmd/bmd/main.go) only reports Motion during an actual button-held drag, so this cleanly distinguishes the two gestures.

(b) ANSI corruption on back-navigation: reproduced by simulating press+drag-motion (setting v.mouseRow/mouseCol) then two loadFileNoHistory calls (payments.md, then back to overview.md, mirroring Ctrl+B) — the returned line showed `\x1b[38;5\x1b[7m;\x1b[m39m` in place of the intact `\x1b[38;5;39m` link color code. Root cause: the mouse-hover-cursor overlay (internal/tui/viewer.go ~line 1932) called insertCursorAt(), which slices the line at a raw rune index with zero ANSI awareness — landing mid-escape-sequence corrupts it exactly like the OSC-image bug in bmd-fbq. Fixed by switching to the already-existing ANSI-aware insertCursorAtVisual() (used correctly elsewhere for edit-mode cursor rendering); deleted the now-dead insertCursorAt().

While reproducing (b), also found that loadFile/loadFileNoHistory never reset hasCursor/selection state across file navigation (unlike BackToDirectory, which got this exact fix under CR-01) — stale selection coordinates from a drag on the old document were corrupting the newly-loaded document's render via highlightTextRangeWithStripped. Fixed by clearing hasCursor, selection state, and the new pendingLinkURL/mouseDragged fields in both loadFile and loadFileNoHistory, matching the CR-01 precedent.

Added 3 regression tests in internal/tui/mouse_test.go: plain-click-still-follows, drag-over-link-selects-instead, and hover-cursor-survives-back-navigation-without-escape-leak. Full suite green, go vet clean, gofmt clean on all changed files.

title: Directory browser split-pane rendering is visually broken
description: Split-pane directory browser view (bmd --browse, wide terminal) renders with severe layout corruption: file list column overlaps/misaligns with content preview pane, stray floating filenames (alerts.md, auth.md) appear detached at top-right outside the normal split boundary, and the content preview area is mostly blank. Screenshot captured during manual verification of v1.1 (test-data/singlerepo-referenced-docs). Likely in internal/tui/directory.go's renderSplitPane/renderDirectoryListingSplit/renderFilePreviewSplit.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. `bmd --browse test-data/singlerepo-referenced-docs` in a wide terminal (split-pane auto-enables at width >= 80).
2. Navigate the file list.
Result: layout is corrupted — file list column overlaps content pane, some filenames (alerts.md, auth.md) render detached/floating outside the normal column boundaries, content preview mostly blank. See screenshot from manual v1.1 verification session.

## Acceptance Criteria
Split-pane directory browser renders with a clean, non-overlapping file-list column and content-preview column at typical terminal widths (e.g. 100-200 cols); no stray/misplaced filenames outside the file-list column.
close_reason: Root cause: renderFilePreviewSplit's preview lines passed through ansiPadOrTruncate (viewer.go), which only recognizes CSI (\x1b[) escapes. Inline images render via renderImage() as OSC 1337 (\x1b]) sequences carrying a giant base64 payload embedded directly in the line text; ansiPadOrTruncate truncated these mid-stream, leaving an unterminated escape sequence that corrupted the terminal display (overlapping panes, floating filenames, blank preview) — reproduced deterministically and confirmed via a throwaway repro harness rendering the actual readme.md/sample-image.png fixture. Fix: added Renderer.WithPlainImages() (internal/renderer/renderer.go) forcing alt-text fallback for images; wired into the split-pane preview renderer construction in directory.go. Added regression tests in internal/renderer/renderer_test.go and internal/tui/directory_test.go (the latter verified to fail pre-fix with the exact truncated escape fragment). Filed bmd-uc6 for an analogous but distinct code path (viewWithBrowser's browserOpen split) not covered by this fix.

title: bmd index default DB path doesn't match graph view's hardcoded read path
description: 'bmd index <dir>' with default flags writes to <dir>/.bmd/knowledge.db (internal/knowledge/commands.go's defaultDBPath, also used by cross-search). internal/tui/graph.go's NewGraphModel hardcodes filepath.Join(rootPath, "knowledge.db") - no .bmd/ prefix. Worse than just 'not found': knowledge.OpenDB() doesn't error on a missing file, SQLite auto-creates an empty one at that path, so the graph view silently renders 0 nodes with no error message. Confirmed pre-existing (git show 760be57^ has the identical hardcoded path), not introduced by Phase 32. Discovered/confirmed via manual smoke testing against the real binary.
acceptance_criteria: NewGraphModel reads from the same defaultDBPath convention (.bmd/knowledge.db) that bmd index's default and cross-search already use, so 'bmd index <dir>' (no --db override) works for graph view too.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. bmd index <dir>  (default flags, writes <dir>/.bmd/knowledge.db)
2. bmd --browse <dir>, press g to open graph view.
Result: graph view silently creates an empty <dir>/knowledge.db via SQLite auto-create and renders 0 nodes, no error shown.
close_reason: Exported knowledge.defaultDBPath as DefaultDBPath; NewGraphModel now uses it instead of a hardcoded rootPath/knowledge.db. Fixed the graph_test.go fixture to match. Full suite green.

title: Mouse clicks bypass activeChild routing, can silently corrupt Viewer file state
description: tea.MouseMsg is never routed through v.activeChild the way tea.KeyMsg/tea.WindowSizeMsg are (viewer.go ~901-903). Combined with v.links never being cleared in BackToDirectory()/BackToSearchResults(), an ordinary mouse click while browsing directory/search/graph can silently trigger followLink()->loadFile() against a stale link from the previously-open file. Viewer.FilePath/Doc/history get swapped with no visible change on screen since the child model still owns View(). Reachable through completely ordinary use (open a file, go back, click anywhere in the listing), not a contrived edge case. Full detail + fix sketch in .planning/phases/32-tui-mode-decoupling-directory-browser-cross-search/32-REVIEW.md (CR-01).
acceptance_criteria: tea.MouseMsg routes through v.activeChild when one is active, matching KeyMsg/WindowSizeMsg. v.links (and v.hasCursor) cleared in BackToDirectory()/BackToSearchResults() so stale link state can't outlive the file view it was built for.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Launch bmd, open a file from the directory listing (Enter).
2. Press h to go back to the directory listing.
3. Left-click anywhere on the listing whose screen row happens to align with one of the previously-open file's link line offsets.
Result: Viewer.FilePath/Doc silently swap to the stale link's target with no visible change on screen.
close_reason: tea.MouseMsg now routes through v.activeChild.Update() before falling through to file-view click handling, matching KeyMsg/WindowSizeMsg. v.links/v.hasCursor cleared in BackToDirectory/BackToSearchResults as defense-in-depth. Regression test added (fails without fix, passes with it). Full suite green.

title: Implement Unicode half-block image rendering for Alacritty and Terminal.app
description:
Research this session (arewesixelyet.com, alacritty/alacritty#910, rasterm, viu, pixterm, chafa) confirmed that mainline Alacritty and macOS Terminal.app have ZERO native inline-image protocol support (no Sixel, no Kitty graphics, no iTerm2 OSC 1337) -- this isn't a detection problem, it's a real capability gap. The two prior fixes this session (bmd-qmb and its correction) stopped bmd from wrongly guessing a protocol these terminals don't support (which printed raw escape sequences as garbage text), falling back to a plain '[Image: alt]' text stub instead.

'First-class support' for these terminals means implementing what bmd's own ProtocolUnicode path was always supposed to be per its doc comment ('Unicode block character representation... fallback that works in any terminal') but which was actually just a stub returning alt text: a real half-block image renderer, the same technique used by pixterm/viu/chafa's fallback mode -- sample 2 vertical pixels per terminal cell, render the U+2584 lower-half-block character with background=top-pixel-color and foreground=bottom-pixel-color via truecolor ANSI SGR codes.

Scope:
1. Decode PNG/JPEG/GIF image bytes into pixel data using Go stdlib (image, image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif) -- no new external dependency.
2. Box-average downsample the decoded image to the target terminal column/row grid, accounting for the ~2:1 height:width aspect ratio of a terminal character cell.
3. Emit half-block ANSI art using 24-bit truecolor SGR codes (both Alacritty and modern Terminal.app support truecolor text rendering, even without any image protocol).
4. Replace the ImageToUnicode() stub with this real renderer, and make it the first attempt in ImageToTerminal's ProtocolUnicode case (falling back to save-temp-file+alt-text only on decode failure).
5. Rewire DetectImageProtocol() so Alacritty and Apple_Terminal (both currently wrongly routed to protocols they do not support) resolve to ProtocolUnicode, which is now a real, working rendering path rather than a last-resort stub.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a document with a local PNG/JPEG image in Alacritty (real Alacritty, TERM=xterm-256color or TERM=alacritty) renders a recognizable half-block ANSI-art approximation of the image, not a text placeholder and not a raw/garbled escape sequence. Same for macOS Terminal.app. Existing Kitty/iTerm2/Sixel-capable terminals are unaffected (still get their native protocol).
notes:
## Thumbnail sizing (same session, final tuning per user visual feedback)

User tested the new kitten test image (bmd-1ii's block-art rendering finally showed a clearly recognizable, well-colored image -- confirms the dithering fix works well for its intended content type: bold shapes/flat colors, as opposed to dense text) and asked whether shrinking it would look better, since it was dominating the document (50 of 58 total lines).

Agreed and implemented: ProtocolUnicode now gets a smaller target width than native protocols specifically -- 40% of terminal width clamped to [20,50] cols (vs native protocols' 60%/[20,100]) -- reasoning: (1) a dithered dot pattern reads more cleanly at a smaller size, similar to halftone newsprint looking smoother at normal viewing distance than up close, (2) block-art has a hard resolution ceiling anyway (confirmed earlier this session) so a large render adds scroll-heavy document real estate without adding legibility for anything with fine detail, (3) native protocols (Kitty/iTerm2/Sixel) don't have this trade-off since width is just a cell-sizing hint for a real raster image, so they keep their original sizing.

Verified: the kitten image at the new ~25-row thumbnail size remains clearly recognizable (round head shape, flower cluster distinctly visible) via an ASCII proxy render. Test renamed TestRenderImage_UnicodeProtocolStaysDocumentProportional -> TestRenderImage_UnicodeProtocolIsThumbnailSized, now asserting ~25 rows (not ~50) at a 180-col terminal. Full suite green, go vet/gofmt clean.

This closes out the bmd-1ii feature: Alacritty/Terminal.app get a real, correctly-dithered, appropriately-sized Braille block-art image preview.
close_reason:
Implemented a real Unicode half-block image renderer (internal/renderer/halfblock.go), the same technique pixterm/viu/chafa use as their universal terminal-agnostic fallback: box-average-downsample the decoded image (stdlib image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif -- no new dependency) to the target column/row grid (accounting for the ~2:1 terminal cell aspect ratio), then emit U+2584 lower-half-block glyphs per cell with truecolor ANSI SGR codes (background=top pixel, foreground=bottom pixel).

Wired in three places:
1. ImageToUnicode() now calls the real renderer, falling back to the old '[Image: alt]' text stub only on decode failure.
2. ImageToTerminal()'s ProtocolUnicode case tries real rendering first, falling back to save-temp-file+alt-text only on decode failure.
3. DetectImageProtocol() no longer guesses Kitty for Alacritty or iTerm2-protocol for Apple_Terminal/generic macOS Terminal matches (both confirmed via research this session to have zero native image-protocol support -- alacritty/alacritty#910 open since 2021, arewesixelyet.com) -- both now route to ProtocolUnicode, which is a real working renderer rather than a last-resort stub. Real iTerm2/Kitty/WezTerm/Sixel detection is unchanged.

Verified against the actual test-data/singlerepo-referenced-docs/sample-image.png fixture: decodes cleanly, produces 19 rows x 60 cols with 94 distinct sampled colors (no degenerate/uniform output), no panics. 9 new tests in internal/renderer/halfblock_test.go covering decode success/failure, row-count-matches-aspect-ratio, ImageToUnicode/ImageToTerminal wiring, and DetectImageProtocol for Alacritty/Apple_Terminal/real-iTerm2. Also corrected stale ProtocolCapabilities() labels that wrongly claimed Alacritty supports Kitty and Terminal.app supports iTerm2. Full suite green, go vet/gofmt clean.

title: Image protocol detection misidentifies non-Terminal.app xterm-TERM terminals as no-image-support
description:
Found via manual testing (user's terminal showed the ProtocolNone '[Image: alt (filename)]' text fallback instead of rendering an inline image). User's actual terminal is Alacritty (confirmed via process-ancestry inspection), configured with TERM=xterm-256color for compatibility rather than the 'alacritty' terminfo entry.

Root cause: DetectImageProtocol() (internal/renderer/images.go) had an explicit Alacritty check (TERM or COLORTERM containing 'alacritty') that only matches when Alacritty uses its own terminfo. When TERM is instead 'xterm-256color' (a common Alacritty/SSH-compatibility configuration), that check misses and the code falls into a broken heuristic: 'if TERM contains xterm and macOS Terminal.app is installed on disk, assume we are running inside Terminal.app and report no image support.' Checking os.Stat on Terminal.app's fixed install path only proves the app is present on the Mac -- true on virtually every Mac regardless of which terminal is actually running -- it says nothing about the CURRENT process's terminal. Real Terminal.app is already correctly identified earlier via TERM_PROGRAM=="Apple_Terminal", making this later branch dead-wrong logic for every other terminal that reaches it.
acceptance_criteria: A terminal reporting TERM=xterm-256color with no recognized TERM_PROGRAM/ITERM_PROGRAM/KITTY_WINDOW_ID/COLORTERM value is treated the same on macOS as elsewhere (guesses ProtocolKitty), not assumed to be Terminal.app with no image support.
notes:
## Correction (same session, found via live user testing)

The first fix (guessing ProtocolKitty for any unrecognized xterm-family TERM) was itself wrong: the user's actual terminal is Alacritty, which does NOT support the Kitty graphics protocol. Guessing Kitty caused Alacritty to print the raw, unrendered Kitty escape sequence (base64 payload and all) as literal garbage text on screen — worse than the original bug's clean alt-text fallback.

Corrected: removed the Kitty guess entirely for the ambiguous xterm-family case; it now falls through to the function's existing safe default (ProtocolUnicode — alt text, no protocol-specific escape emitted) rather than gambling on unverified protocol support. Test renamed/updated to assert ProtocolUnicode, not ProtocolKitty, for this case.
close_reason:
Root cause confirmed by inspecting the user's process ancestry (Alacritty.app in the shell's parent chain) plus their TERM=xterm-256color, then reproducing the exact code path: DetectImageProtocol()'s 'if TERM contains xterm, check os.Stat on Terminal.app's install path, assume Terminal.app if present' heuristic is unsound — that path exists on virtually every Mac regardless of the running terminal, and real Terminal.app is already correctly caught earlier via TERM_PROGRAM=="Apple_Terminal". Alacritty configured with TERM=xterm-256color (a common setup for SSH/terminfo compatibility, bypassing the earlier explicit 'alacritty' TERM/COLORTERM check) fell through into this broken branch and was wrongly reported as ProtocolNone.

Fixed by removing the Terminal.app disk-existence check entirely; xterm-family TERM values with no other recognized signal now guess ProtocolKitty on macOS too, matching the behavior already used for non-macOS xterm-256color terminals.

Added TestDetectImageProtocol_XtermTermWithoutTermProgram_NotAssumedTerminalApp (internal/renderer/renderer_test.go), verified via revert-and-rerun: fails against the old code with 'got 0' (ProtocolNone), passes with the fix. Full suite green, go vet/gofmt clean.

title: Unguarded narrow-width truncation panics (slice bounds out of range)
description: directory.go's renderDirectoryListing header and graph.go's truncateLabel both subtract a fixed margin before slicing with no floor guard (unlike splitPaneWidths()'s existing <80/<20 checks). directory.go panics when DirectoryModel.width < 3 (headerRunes[:m.width-3] goes negative). graph.go's truncateLabel panics when maxWidth < 1 for any non-empty title (called with width-8 and width-12 args). Full detail + fix sketch in .planning/phases/32-tui-mode-decoupling-directory-browser-cross-search/32-REVIEW.md (CR-02).
acceptance_criteria: Floor guards added before both slice operations; no panic for any terminal width >= 1.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Launch bmd in a terminal narrower than 3 columns (directory.go) or resize a graph view to width < 8-12 columns depending on label length (graph.go truncateLabel).
Result: panic: slice bounds out of range.
close_reason: Added floor guards: directory.go nameMaxWidth clamped to >=1 (also fixed a second unguarded slice beyond the ticket's header-only description, reachable at width ~20-30 with long filenames); graph.go truncateLabel returns empty for maxWidth<1 and skips ellipsis for 1<=maxWidth<3. Regression tests added, verified to panic without the fix, full suite green.

title: Phase 33: Clipboard & Live Reload
description: Native OS clipboard fallback alongside OSC52 (view mode and edit mode) for terminals without OSC52 support. View mode detects external file changes on disk (fsnotify) and reloads, matching glow's behavior. Must not disrupt edit mode / unsaved changes.
design: Requirements: CLIP-01, RELOAD-01. Independent of phases 31/32/34 — small, low-risk, self-contained.
acceptance_criteria: Copy succeeds via native OS clipboard fallback when OSC52 unsupported; OSC52 path unregressed where supported. View mode auto-reloads on external file change; edit mode with unsaved changes is never disrupted by an external change.
close_reason: Both CLIP-01 (native clipboard fallback) and RELOAD-01 (fsnotify live-reload) implemented, tested, and committed. Full test suite green, gofmt clean.

title: Phase 32: TUI Mode Decoupling (Directory Browser & Cross-Search)
description: Directory-browser and cross-document-search modes become independent Bubble Tea child models communicating with the parent Viewer via messages, not shared boolean flags and direct method calls — mirroring glow's stashModel -> fetchedMarkdownMsg -> pagerModel composition pattern. OpenFileFromDirectory currently calls straight into Viewer.loadFile(); mode-transition flags (splitMode, graphMode, helpOpen) are shared across the directory<->graph<->help<->cross-search boundary.
design: HIGHEST-RISK phase this milestone — deferred twice already this session for exactly this reason. Must include an explicit design pass on the parent/child message boundary (what crosses as a message vs. what stays shared) BEFORE any code changes — see PROJECT.md Context and ROADMAP.md Phase 32 Note. Requirements: ARCH-01, ARCH-02, ARCH-03.
acceptance_criteria: Directory-browser and cross-search state live in their own model types with their own Update/render logic, not flat Viewer fields. File selection produces a tea.Cmd/tea.Msg the parent handles, not a direct loadFile() call. All existing directory-browser/cross-search functionality behaves identically (existing tests + manual smoke test pass).
close_reason: Phase 32 complete: all 4 plans executed, verified, UAT signed off. Follow-ups filed as bmd-51c/db6/2y3/0fe/js5.

title: Simplify BM25 SQLite persistence (documents/index_entries tables)
description: bmd query and SearchAllDocuments used to call db.LoadIndex() and immediately discard the result via a full rescan+rebuild (db only stores metadata, not content, so snippets always require a rescan). That wasteful call was removed in bmd-201's follow-up cleanup (session 2026-08-02). SaveIndex/LoadIndex and the documents/index_entries/bm25_stats tables in db.go still exist and are tested, and SaveIndex remains load-bearing for IsIndexStale's staleness detection. Open question: is it worth keeping the BM25 postings tables at all if nothing ever loads them back for search, or should the schema be trimmed to just what staleness-detection needs (built_at + documents id/path/mtime)? Needs a decision, not just deletion — touches db.go schema/migrations.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) BM25 postings persistence is removed from the schema and staleness detection is reworked to not depend on it, or (b) a decision is documented that the current schema is fine to keep as-is for potential future use.

title: viewWithBrowser split-view has same unclippable inline-image corruption as bmd-fbq
description: viewer.go's viewWithBrowser() (toggled via v.browserOpen, a legacy in-viewer file-browser split distinct from the bmd --browse DirectoryModel) truncates the main content column to mainWidth via padOrTruncate (viewer.go:1974), which does raw byte slicing with no ANSI/OSC awareness at all. If the viewed document contains an inline image, renderImage() emits an OSC 1337 (iTerm2)/Sixel escape sequence embedded directly in the line text (see internal/renderer/renderer.go renderImage). Byte-truncating that mid-sequence leaves an unterminated escape that will corrupt the terminal exactly like bmd-fbq did for the split-pane directory browser (bmd-fbq was fixed by adding Renderer.WithPlainImages(), forcing alt-text fallback in any sub-column render path). This path was not covered by the bmd-fbq fix since it's a separate code path (Viewer.browserOpen vs DirectoryModel.splitMode) and wasn't the one reproduced in the original bug report.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a document containing an inline image while the in-viewer browser split (browserOpen) is active never emits a raw/truncated image escape sequence into the rendered output; likely fix is the same WithPlainImages() renderer option applied wherever viewWithBrowser constructs its renderer.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open a markdown document containing an inline image (e.g. test-data/singlerepo-referenced-docs/readme.md) with bmd in normal (non --browse) mode.
2. Toggle the in-viewer file browser split (v.browserOpen — check keybinding in viewer.go, search for where it's set to true, e.g. around lines 877/885).
3. With the image-containing doc as the main content, the main column gets byte-truncated via padOrTruncate(mainLine, mainWidth) at viewer.go:1974, with no ANSI/OSC escape awareness.
Expected: same class of terminal corruption as bmd-fbq (truncated OSC 1337 escape sequence, unterminated, garbling subsequent rendering) since this uses a non-ANSI-aware raw byte truncation (padOrTruncate), which is actually more naive than the ansiPadOrTruncate used in the already-fixed directory.go path.

## Fix approach
Apply the same Renderer.WithPlainImages() fix used for bmd-fbq (internal/renderer/renderer.go) to whichever renderer construction feeds viewWithBrowser's main content, forcing alt-text fallback instead of inline image escapes in this sub-column view.
close_reason:
Fixed the same escape-corruption class as bmd-fbq, but via a different mechanism since this path (viewWithBrowser) shares v.Lines with the normal full-screen view — it can't just re-render with WithPlainImages() without breaking real inline images in that other view, and re-rendering v.Doc at the narrower mainWidth would desync v.Offset-based scrolling (different wrap width means different line counts).

Instead: added stripInlineImageEscapes() (internal/tui/viewer.go), which scans a line for OSC (\x1b]) sequences terminated by BEL or ST and replaces each whole match with a plain '[image]' placeholder, applied to the main content line before truncation. Also replaced the byte-truncating padOrTruncate (now dead, deleted) with the already-ANSI-aware ansiPadOrTruncate at the same call site, so any other embedded CSI color codes survive truncation intact too, not just images.

Verified by reverting the fix and re-running the new regression test (TestViewWithBrowser_InlineImage_NoRawEscapeLeak, internal/tui/viewer_test.go): it fails against the old code with the exact truncated fragment '\x1b]1337;File=name=image.png;size=47;width=60;height=40;inline=1;p│' bleeding into the rendered frame, and passes with the fix. Full suite green, go vet/gofmt clean.

title: Flaky test: TestScanConfig_IgnoreFilesPatterns fails intermittently under full package run
description: Discovered while verifying an unrelated fix (bmd-0fe) in internal/knowledge/scanner_test.go. TestScanConfig_IgnoreFilesPatterns passes consistently in isolation (go test -run TestScanConfig_IgnoreFilesPatterns) but fails intermittently (~1 in 3 runs observed) when the full internal/knowledge package suite runs together (go test ./internal/knowledge/... -count=1), with 'draft.md (lowercase) should be included, only DRAFT.md is ignored'. Symptom suggests shared/global state (possibly a package-level ignore-pattern cache, cwd, or test ordering dependency) leaking between tests rather than a real scanner bug. Not investigated further — out of scope for the bug fixes in progress at the time.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `go test ./internal/knowledge/... -count=1` several times in a row (observed failing ~1 in 3 runs).
2. Failure: `scanner_test.go:449: draft.md (lowercase) should be included, only DRAFT.md is ignored`
3. Running `go test ./internal/knowledge/... -run TestScanConfig_IgnoreFilesPatterns -count=1` in isolation always passes — confirms this is a cross-test interaction, not a real scanner bug.

## Acceptance Criteria
`go test ./internal/knowledge/... -count=1` passes consistently across repeated runs (e.g. 10/10), with no test-ordering-dependent failures in TestScanConfig_IgnoreFilesPatterns.
close_reason: Root cause: TestScanConfig_IgnoreFilesPatterns created both draft.md and DRAFT.md via createTestTree's map[string]string in one call, which collide onto a single directory entry on case-insensitive-but-case-preserving filesystems (default macOS APFS/HFS+) - Go's randomized map iteration order nondeterministically decided which write won, flipping whether the ignore pattern matched. Split the case-sensitive-match assertion into its own isolated test with no colliding sibling file. Verified 8/8 clean runs (was ~1/3 failure rate before).

title: switchModeMsg{modeDirectory} error path silently swallowed
description: When restoring/creating a DirectoryModel fails in Viewer.Update()'s switchModeMsg{modeDirectory} handler (viewer.go ~479-492), the error from NewDirectoryModel is dropped on the floor - no v.errorMsg set, activeChild left unchanged, user gets no feedback. The sibling modeGraph branch two cases above it correctly surfaces errors via v.errorMsg + clearErrorAfter. Detail in 32-REVIEW.md (WR-01).
acceptance_criteria: NewDirectoryModel error surfaces via v.errorMsg + clearErrorAfter, matching the modeGraph branch's pattern.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Get into a state where DirectoryModel construction can fail (e.g. rootPath became unreadable/deleted mid-session) while switching modes back to modeDirectory.
Result: no error shown, activeChild left unchanged, screen looks unresponsive.
close_reason: modeDirectory branch of switchModeMsg now surfaces NewDirectoryModel's error via v.errorMsg + clearErrorAfter, mirroring the modeGraph branch's existing pattern exactly. No unit test added: NewDirectoryModel's error paths (filepath.Abs / WalkDir) are not reliably forceable without a disproportionate test seam - confirmed via scratch testing that WalkDir's error-swallowing callback means neither a missing nor non-directory root path currently produces an error. Full suite green.

title: Phase 34: Rendering Evaluation Spike
description: Produce a concrete, evidence-based recommendation on bmd's markdown rendering approach: keep the custom internal/renderer, adopt glamour+chroma fully, or hybrid (chroma for code blocks only). Backed by a working prototype for code-block syntax highlighting. This is a spike/evaluation deliverable, NOT a committed rewrite of internal/renderer.
design: Requirements: RENDER-01. Scope guardrail: recommendation + prototype only, a full rendering-engine swap (even if recommended) belongs in a future milestone, not v1.1.
acceptance_criteria: Working prototype renders at least one real doc's code blocks with chroma highlighting, runnable independently of production render path. Written recommendation compares the 3 options against concrete criteria (visual quality, binary size, performance, maintenance) with a clear next step. internal/renderer production path is untouched by the spike. If glamour/chroma is recommended, follow-up implementation scope is written up.
close_reason: Both plans executed and verified (9/9 must-haves, 34-VERIFICATION.md). Recommendation: keep bmd's custom internal/renderer as-is — driven by glamour v1.0.0's verified structural lack of image-protocol/link-sentinel support (D-01 hard blocker), not by secondary factors (binary size +2.64MB, visual quality comparable, bmd ~10-11% faster in benchmarks — all roughly a wash). Deliverable at cmd/render-spike/RECOMMENDATION.md on branch spike/render-glamour-eval (never merged into main, never pushed). No follow-up implementation scoped. Full v1.1 milestone now complete (4/4 phases).

title: Dead ASCII graph-diagram renderer: fix cycle handling or delete
description: RenderGraphASCII/renderGraphWithForceLayout/forceDirectedLayout/computeNodeLayout are fully written and unit-tested in graph.go but never called from the real View() path (renderFocusedSubgraph's list view is what's actually shown). Investigated wiring it up as the default; found a real bug first: computeNodeLayout's level-assignment relaxation assumes a DAG with zero cycle detection. On a cyclic graph (extremely common for interlinked markdown docs, e.g. a.md<->b.md), the relaxation never converges, node levels blow up (measured maxCol=1288 on a 200-node realistic graph vs expected ~0-1), and nodes land off-canvas and vanish silently with no error - 27.5% node loss measured in testing. The 40-node safety fallback to list view works correctly and is not itself buggy. Decision needed: (1) delete the dead code as a cleanup, or (2) fix the layout algorithm (proper cycle-aware leveling/compaction) and wire it up as a real diagram view, or (3) leave as untouched dead code (status quo).
design: Recommend (1) delete unless the diagram feature is specifically wanted enough to justify (2)'s real algorithmic work.
notes:
## Acceptance Criteria
Either: RenderGraphASCII/renderGraphWithForceLayout/forceDirectedLayout/computeNodeLayout and their tests are removed, and graph.go no longer carries unused rendering code; OR: computeNodeLayout gains cycle-aware leveling/compaction so cyclic graphs (e.g. a.md<->b.md) don't lose nodes off-canvas, and the diagram is wired up as View()'s real output (behind a toggle or as the new default).
close_reason: Deleted the dead code per the ticket's own recommendation: RenderGraphASCII/renderGraphWithForceLayout/forceDirectedLayout/computeNodeLayout, supporting types/consts, the write-only GraphViewState.NodeLayout field, and all tests that existed only to exercise them (net -1130 lines). GraphModel.View() always rendered via renderFocusedSubgraph, which is untouched. Full suite green, gofmt clean.
